articleTitle: Computation Offloading and Resource Allocation in MEC-enabled Vehicular Networks: Partial Offloading Versus Binary Offloading
publicationTitle: 2024 7th World Conference on Computing and Communication Technologies (WCCCT)
abstract: By allowing vehicle terminals (VTs) to offload computation tasks to edge servers, mobile edge computing (MEC) effectively alleviates the computational burden on VTs and improves system latency performance in vehicular networks. In this paper, we investigate joint computation offloading and resource allocation problem with different offloading schemes, i.e, partial offloading and binary offloading. We formulate optimization problems to minimize the task completion latency, and obtain the optimal computation offloading and resource allocation solutions. With both offloading schemes, computation offloading and resource allocation algorithms are developed. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed algorithms exhibit significant latency performance advantages over the benchmark schemes. Additionally, the performances of two offloading schemes are also compared, the results show that partial offloading scheme outperforms binary offloading in latency performances.

articleTitle: A Multi-scale Feature Embedding Extension Network for RGB-D Cross-modal Person Re-identification
publicationTitle: 2024 7th World Conference on Computing and Communication Technologies (WCCCT)
abstract: The RGB-D cross-modal person re-identification task is a branch of the cross-modal person re-identification task, aiming to match pedestrian images between RGB and depth modalities. Its main challenge lies in the significant modality difference between RGB and depth images. Due to the limited research attention on this task, there is a lack of large-scale, high-quality training data, making existing methods struggle to capture effective correlational information between RGB and depth modalities. This paper proposes a novel feature embedding expansion network for RGB-D cross-modal person re-identification. The network introduces perturbations to the embedding of intermediate-layer features to generate multiple diversified embedding features, effectively alleviating the problem of limited training data for RGB-D tasks. Simultaneously, through the incorporation of deformable convolution operations and depth-wise separable convolution operations during the embedding feature generation, the model is encouraged to learn richer scale and channel information from the limited training data. Meanwhile, by controlling the distance between expanded feature embeddings and original feature embeddings for different modalities, we mitigate the significant modality differences. Experimental results on the public benchmark datasets BIWI and RobotPKU demonstrate that our approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods.

articleTitle: Content Based Email Spam Filtering and Detection using Hybrid Supervised Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 7th World Conference on Computing and Communication Technologies (WCCCT)
abstract: In today’s world, email is used widely for communication purposes globally. Email spam are unwanted emails that are sent to many recipients receivers. It is usually used for commercial purposes More likely spam enail is also used for malicious attempts to gain access to receiver computer/device. This article presents a novel hybrid architecture for spam emails filtering using mails content-based approach. For filtering, Word2Vec (W2V) word embedding procedure is used for feature selection with bio-inspired “Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO)” and “Support Vector Machine (SVM)” combined with “Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)”. Moreover, our proposed hybrid architecture is simulated in open-source tool and the performance is evaluated using standard confusion matrix. Afterw ards, the results are compared with various previous algorithms/models. Experimental results show that our proposed hybrid scheme enhances detection accuracy of spam emails.

articleTitle: Deep Learning and Kriging
publicationTitle: 2024 7th World Conference on Computing and Communication Technologies (WCCCT)
abstract: Kriging, a geostatistical method for optimal linear prediction, is widely used in various domains including mining, hydrology, and environmental and health sciences, as well as in computational experiments. This technique bears a close resemblance to kernel methods in machine learning. Despite the swift advancement of deep learning techniques, their application in spatial prediction remains relatively underexplored. In this context, we introduce a deep neural network-based approach for spatial prediction, designed to be resilient against variations in both the mean function and the kernel function.

articleTitle: A Novel Phase Shifter for 5G Base Station Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 7th World Conference on Computing and Communication Technologies (WCCCT)
abstract: In this paper, a phase shifter for the base station antenna with low cost, ease of manufacturing and good performance on phase shift is presented. The phase shifter consists of a metal shell, a substrate, two dielectric plates, and two conductor lines. The phase shift is realized by moving the dielectric plates longitudinally, which cover the conductor lines. With the slots in dielectric materials, the slotted part of dielectric plates can function similarly to a quarter-wavelength impedance matching. Therefore, the function of this phase shifter is that the voltage standing wave ratio (VSWR) and power distribution ratio can be guaranteed when the dielectric plate is moved. The phase shifter exhibits a bandwidth of 1.7-2.1 GHz and the corresponding phase shift is 86.88° when the dielectric plate moves by 90 mm. Moreover, its good physical features including light weight, low cost, and easy fabrication make it well suitable for base station antenna applications.

articleTitle: Landmine Detection Based on Faster R-CNN in UAV Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 7th World Conference on Computing and Communication Technologies (WCCCT)
abstract: Landmine detection is not just a technical task, it is also a crucial element in alleviating humanitarian disasters and aiding in the reconstruction of communities living under the threat of landmines. This undertaking not only saves lives but also offers people the opportunity to rebuild stable lives. The integration of drones into this context significantly enhances coverage and safety measures, providing a substantial improvement for thorough and comprehensive landmine target detection with valuable multi-modal data sources. This paper revolves around the pivotal task of capturing and collecting landmine datasets, utilizing images obtained through unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). The model, based on the trained faster region-based convolutional neural network (Faster R-CNN) algorithm, is intended to serve as a valuable tool for subsequent activities such as landmine monitoring, identification, and in-depth analysis, thereby offering reliable recommendations for enhanced decision-making.

articleTitle: Optimization Research for Slot Allocation at Chengdu’s Dual 4F Class Airportsa
publicationTitle: 2024 7th World Conference on Computing and Communication Technologies (WCCCT)
abstract: Chengdu Shuangliu International Airport (CTU) and Tianfu International Airport (TFU) are ranked as 4F, the highest class in world capable of handling wide-body aircraft. Due to a rising demand surpasses these two airports’ existing infrastructure capacity, it is necessary to further study the problem of slot optimization for Chengdu’s dual 4F airports. Prior study on slot allocation has focused on a single airport, with little attention paid to Chengdu that consist of two 4F class airports. In this paper, we systematically analyze the slot operational indicators in Chengdu’s dual 4F class airports, including flight frequency and flight distance of major busy routes, hourly flow and capacity utilization, flight time of major busy routes, abnormal flight release rate, and compliance rate of planned connection time at airport of major airlines. This paper proposes an optimization model of slot for airport group according to the status of hourly flow at Chengdu’s dual 4F airports. Computational model simulation shows that the CTU flow decreases and the TFU flow increases during10-19 slots, which reflecting the optimization effect are generally consistent with the needs of travelers.

articleTitle: Emergency Message Propagation Scheme of Cellular Vehicle Networking for High Reliability and Low Delay Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 7th World Conference on Computing and Communication Technologies (WCCCT)
abstract: With the rapid development of vehicle-mounted communication technology, vehicle-mounted ad hoc network (VANET) has attracted more and more attention from academia and industry, supporting many security applications with strict quality of service (QoS) requirements such as low delay, high reliability and scalability. In VANET, the propagation delay and reliability of emergency information are important indicators of these security applications. However, in the urban traffic environment, complex road structure, serious channel competition and message redundancy seriously affect the efficiency of information dissemination, resulting in increased propagation delay and reduced reliability. In order to solve these problems, this paper proposes a message propagation strategy (PDS) based on the selection of dominant nodes in dynamic graph. Experiments show that PDS has good advantages in the performance of dominating nodes and repeatedly dominating nodes. Specifically, compared with MIS algorithm, the number of dominating nodes is reduced by $ 24.7\%$. Compared with FB algorithm, the message propagation delay is reduced by $ 52.2\%$, the message propagation speed is increased by $ 37.3\%$, and the message redundancy is reduced by $ 42.6\%$.

articleTitle: Design of Safety Management System for Training Room Applying Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2024 7th World Conference on Computing and Communication Technologies (WCCCT)
abstract: As a crucial site for practical teaching, safety management in vocational college training rooms is still primarily manual, which is both unsafe and inconvenient. To address this issue, Internet of Things (IoT) technology can be employed to support intelligent management of training rooms. Therefore, a safety management system for training rooms has been designed, utilizing IoT technology. This system’s composition, as well as the design of its software and hardware, will be discussed. The training room management system is designed using sensor technology, ZigBee, and other IoT applications. The system includes hardware, software, and a management platform. Data is communicated wirelessly in real-time through Zigbee technology using a control terminal based on the STM32F103C8 processor. The control program and management platform are designed using C language. The door can be easily opened by swiping the card and starting the training equipment with a single key, using a safety management system that solves some of the disadvantages of manual management.

articleTitle: IBAVOA: An Improved African Vulture Optimization Algorithm for Feature Selection
publicationTitle: 2024 7th World Conference on Computing and Communication Technologies (WCCCT)
abstract: In the domain of machine learning, redundant and irrelevant features will significantly impede a model’s learning ability. However, identifying an effective subset of features from a massive pool of feasible solutions remains a challenge. To address this issue, this paper introduces IBAVOA, an optimization algorithm designed for feature selection. Built upon the excellent performance of the African Vulture Optimization Algorithm, this algorithm enhances its capabilities through initialization with tent map, an adaptive quasi-oppositional mutation strategy, and the S-shaped function. Comparative experiments conducted on six datasets from UCI repository against five popular optimization algorithms demonstrate that this algorithm can effectively reduce feature dimensions while simultaneously achieving a better classification accuracy.

articleTitle: An End-to-end Online DDoS Mitigation Scheme for Network Forwarding Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 7th World Conference on Computing and Communication Technologies (WCCCT)
abstract: The past decade has witnessed continuous development of IoT, 5G, and AI technologies, which have driven explosive growth in network bandwidth. The scale and frequency of DDoS (Distributed Denial of Service) attacks are also increasing. In order to expand the scope of attacks, some hackers even targeted the network infrastructures. In this context, the security of network forwarding devices has become a concern. DDoS attacks on network forwarding devices cannot be mitigated by traffic diversion and scrubbing. However, mitigation on-premises faces many problems, including insufficient bandwidth of the channel between the forwarding plane and the control plane, limited computing resources, selection of blocking mode, and a short response window. This paper proposes an adaptive-granularity Attack tRaffic bEhavior Aggregation algorithm - namely AREA - to detect attacks precisely, and utilizes an ACL generation technique to reduce false alarms. During a DDoS attack, the attacker sources are automatically analyzed to implement mitigation. Experiments show the ability of the proposed method to automatically block DDoS attacks with high accuracy, high recall rate, and little false negative rate in an end-to-end manner. Therefore, network forwarding devices remain highly available even during attacks.

articleTitle: Practical Foreground Traffic Performance Modeling for Wide Area Network
publicationTitle: 2024 7th World Conference on Computing and Communication Technologies (WCCCT)
abstract: The quality of service (QoS) in wide area networks (WANs) is crucial for ensuring efficient and reliable communication. Traditional QoS evaluation approaches, such as analysis, simulation, and emulation, have shown limitations in terms of accuracy or computational efficiency. The emergence of the digital twin network paradigm has inspired data-driven schemes that aim to construct accurate and lightweight performance evaluation models. However, practical application of these schemes often encounters challenges due to their heavy dependence on complex and detailed network state information, requiring extensive measurements and reporting overhead. In this paper, we propose a practical data-driven methodology, DT-WAN, that harnesses the power of graph neural networks (GNNs) to model and evaluate QoS in WANs. DT-WAN addresses the challenge of reducing measurement complexity by focusing on foreground traffic QoS, while considering the impact of background flows with minimal information collection. Through simulation experiments, we demonstrate that DT-WAN achieves accurate prediction of QoS distributions for foreground traffic, with low Wasserstein distance.

articleTitle: A Horizontal Omnidirectional Broadband Antenna for the LTE/5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 7th World Conference on Computing and Communication Technologies (WCCCT)
abstract: Due to the growing demand of a large number of users for large amounts of data transmission, the LTE/5G communication system will require its antenna to have an omnidirectional radiation mode and a wide frequency bandwidth. In this study, a novel omnidirectional horizontally polarized antenna for the LTE/5G communication system is proposed. The antenna consists of three pairs of arc dipoles, six pairs of parasitic strip lines, and several cross-type elliptic patches, aiming at the extension of the antenna’s bandwidth. To achieve the antenna configured miniaturization, a design method that integrates the feed network with the antenna is adopted. The simulated result exhibits a −10-dB frequency bandwidth of 1.72-3.75 GHz (74.2%). It also achieves a satisfactory horizontal omnidirectional pattern in the horizontal mode, with a peak gain of 5.21 dBi. Furthermore, the proposed antenna has a small size of $120 \times 120 \times 0.8128 \mathrm{~mm}^{3}$, with a low profile of $0.688 \lambda_{\text {min }}$ (where $\lambda_{\text {min }}$ is the free space wavelength at the minimum working frequency).

articleTitle: Optimal Power Allocation of Energy Efficiency for Cognitive Relaying Networks with Nakagami-m Fading Channels
publicationTitle: 2024 7th World Conference on Computing and Communication Technologies (WCCCT)
abstract: Energy efficiency optimization of wireless communication systems has attracted increasing attention recently due to its beneficial impacts on the environment and operational savings. In this work, we present a power allocation framework for cognitive relaying networks based on maximizing the energy efficiency (EE). First, we show that the relation between the EE and the spectral efficiency (SE) is strictly increasing in single user communication system. In addition, we solve a nonconvex problem and explicitly derive the optimal power for the proposed average energy efficiency under peak transmit power and peak interference power constraints. Finally, we apply our results to the cognitive relaying networks, in which the power is limited by an interference constraint with Nakagami-m fading channels. Simulation results show that optimal power allocation can significant improving energy efficiency of cognitive relaying networks.

articleTitle: Depression Detection Based On Text And User Networksa
publicationTitle: 2024 7th World Conference on Computing and Communication Technologies (WCCCT)
abstract: The extensive utilization of social networks presented an opportunity for detecting depression in a timely and cost-effective manner. In that paper, we proposed TUNDD, a depression detection method based on text and user network, which leveraged social network data. TUNDD comprised three modules: the text embedding module utilized BERT to encode post text, the graph perception module applied GAT to explore potential relationships among users, and the classification module combined post text and user vectors, transforming them into higher-dimensional vectors through BiRNN and generating results through softmax. Experimental results demonstrated that TUNDD outperformed five baseline experiments on two datasets, achieving accuracy rates of 86.3% and 84.7%, respectively. Furthermore, ablation experiments revealed that BERT, GAT, and the number of neural network layers in GAT significantly impacted the effectiveness of depression detection.

articleTitle: A CH9 Low-Profile Circularly-Polarized Antenna for Indoor Positioning
publicationTitle: 2024 7th World Conference on Computing and Communication Technologies (WCCCT)
abstract: This paper presents a low-profile CH9 circularly polarized 3-element multiple input multiple output (MIMO) antenna for precise positioning applications. The feeding structure of the antenna employs a conventional wilkinson power divider to achieve circular polarization, where the feeding structure and the radiating patch are located on the same layer of the dielectric substrate with a grounded backside. The −10-dB bandwidth of each antenna element ranges from 7.04 to 8.55 GHz, with a gain larger than 2.21 dBi within the desired bandwidth. In order to enhance localization accuracy and minimize the impact of spatial correlation, the distance interval between antenna elements is designed to be 12.5 mm. Experimental results show that when ports 1, 2 and 3 are excited with equal amplitude phase differences of 0 °, 90 ° and −90 °, respectively, the frequency bandwidth of the MIMO antenna is ranging from 7.61 to 8.48 GHz, with corresponding gain fluctuating from 5.39 to 8.07 dBi. In addition, the circularly polarized bandwidth is from 7 to 8.89 GHz, which fully covers the CH9 frequency band.

articleTitle: Online Assignment of Satellite Data Transmission Tasks Based on Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient
publicationTitle: 2024 7th World Conference on Computing and Communication Technologies (WCCCT)
abstract: This study focuses on the scheduling problem of satellite data transmission tasks, where ground station resources are scarce and subject to multiple constraints, such as limited funding, long investment cycles, and limited industrial technology. With the increase of satellite observation tasks, data transmission tasks continue to rise, making scheduling problems more urgent. Effective data transmission task scheduling requires comprehensive consideration of multiple factors such as task priority, visible time window, and ground station location within a limited time frame, in order to maximize the utilization of ground station resources and ensure the effective and efficient execution of satellite data transmission tasks. In addition, considering the segmentation and rearrangement capabilities of satellites and the need for online scheduling of emergency data transmission tasks, this paper proposes a new online scheduling problem for data transmission tasks (OSDTT). To solve the OSDTT problem, deep reinforcement learning method was introduced, and online scheduling of dynamic data transmission tasks was achieved through Markov modeling and deep deterministic policy gradient algorithm. The experimental results show that the proposed algorithm performs superior on the OSDTT problem. Overall, this study provides a new perspective and solution for satellite data transmission task scheduling problems, emphasizing the importance of online scheduling for dynamic tasks. In addition, it contributes to the improvement of algorithm performance in different task density scenarios.

Author Keywords: twin delayed deep deterministic policy gradient

articleTitle: Ring-PPFL: A Ring Topology based Framework for Privacy-Preserving Federated Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 7th World Conference on Computing and Communication Technologies (WCCCT)
abstract: Federated learning enables collaborative model training while preventing the centralization of data, thus ensuring data privacy. However, the potential leakage of model updates poses privacy risks. In this paper, we propose Ring-PPFL, a framework based on ring topology and double masks, to improve privacy preservation in federated learning. Specifically, Ring-PPFL adopts a ring communication mechanism to transmit local model parameters and uses a double-mask mechanism of two independent masks (one provided by the server and another by a trusted third party) in the communication to defend against collusion attacks. Experiments on MNIST and CIFAR-100 show that the model accuracy and convergence speed of Ring-PPFL are comparable to FedAvg, and the model accuracy is 10%-60% higher than differential privacy. At the same time, the GML value of Ring-PPFL is about 60 times higher than that of differential privacy using larger noise (1e-1); that is, the privacy preservation capability of Ring-PPFL is better than that of differential privacy. Our framework provides a feasible solution for deploying federated learning with enhanced privacy preservation.

articleTitle: Research on Time Compensation of Cooperative Tracking for UAVs Swarm
publicationTitle: 2024 7th World Conference on Computing and Communication Technologies (WCCCT)
abstract: Due to complex structure, flexibility and strong mobility of UAVs swarm, the existing time registration model of Cooperative Tracking can not effectively perform the time error compensation task for the trajectory of drone swarm. In this paper, clustering and approximate entropy are used as preprocessing steps in the auxiliary decision making of anti-UAVs swarm system firstly, then BP network and Kalman filtering are combined to complete the time compensation task. Experiment results show that, based on the improved auxiliary decision making method, the adaptive time registration model can perform better in accuracy and speed compared with the method fully using Kalman filtering.

articleTitle: The dynamic job assignment problem in grid computing: A comparative study of two optimization methods
publicationTitle: 2024 7th World Conference on Computing and Communication Technologies (WCCCT)
abstract: The advent of the Software Defined Networking (SDN) and Network Function Virtualization (NFV) technologies in the field of telecommunications has led to a tremendous reduction of costs as well as an increase in terms of infrastructure flexibility. Thus, equipments that play a pivotal role in telecommunications have merely been replaced by computers and their functions have accordingly been softwarized. To further reduce costs, some telecommunications carriers are now considering using decentralized grid computing-based networks to route a part of their traffic. The user-PC computer system (UPC) system is a technology for pooling and making available the unused computing resources (CPU) of the personal computers (PC) of members belonging to the same organization. For instance, in the drug discovery, economic forecasting, seismic analysis fields that deal with computationally intensive problem solving, Grid Computing has become an essential tool for building an affordable computing environment. We have previously designed an efficient static job scheduling genetic algorithm considering CPU core utilization for the UPC system. It finds an optimal assignment that minimizes the processing time of the available set of jobs in a static scenario, i.e., jobs are all available in the beginning and all worker PCs are idle. However, in reality, jobs join and leave the system dynamically and therefore, when new jobs join the system, some workers may be busy. In this paper, we propose an extension of our previously proposed static job scheduling genetic algorithm, that considers dynamic job scheduling in the UPC system. We conducted experiments using six worker PCs and up to 51 jobs. A comparative study of the results obtained using our dynamic scheduling genetic algorithm showed an improvement of about 13.67% in Makespan compared to that of the Dynamic Randomized Multi-Start Local Search (DRMSLS)-based method.

articleTitle: A Survey of Privacy Preserving Methods based on Differential Privacy for Medical Data
publicationTitle: 2024 7th World Conference on Computing and Communication Technologies (WCCCT)
abstract: Using deep learning and federated learning in the medical domain has facilitated convenience in diagnosing and treating patients. However, the current privacy leakage problem has made patients more cautious about personal privacy security. Privacy security has become an urgent issue. Differential privacy is a cryptography technique that makes it impossible for attackers to identify personal data by adding noise to the training process. In this work, we first provide a complete overview of differential privacy technologies. Then, we will review existing differential privacy works in the medical field. Finally, we analyze the existing problems of differential privacy and propose possible avenues for further research.

articleTitle: Graph-based Time-critical Message Dissemination Maximization Scheme for 5G NR-V2X Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 7th World Conference on Computing and Communication Technologies (WCCCT)
abstract: Existing broadcast techniques are challenging to meet the low-latency high-reliability requirements of advanced V2X applications. As an enhancement to broadcast, unicast mode has been introduced in 5G NR-V2X. The strategy of unicast V2V message dissemination is investigated, and the problem of maximizing k-vertex reachable nodes within h-hop is proposed. A maximum matching-based algorithm named HKVR is presented to solve the problem. Experimental results indicate that HKVR has better performance than traditional centrality-based strategies. With a few source nodes, HKVR can achieve 100% coverage for small networks; average hops can be reduced by 33% for large-scale networks with thousands of nodes.

articleTitle: Research on Intelligent Question-Answer System for Tender Information Based on Knowledge Graph
publicationTitle: 2024 7th World Conference on Computing and Communication Technologies (WCCCT)
abstract: Traditional methods of obtaining tender information often rely on manual searches or browsing through large volumes of documents and web pages, resulting in low efficiency and the potential for overlooking important details. Therefore, this paper constructs a knowledge graph for tender information and develops a tender information question-answering system based on the tender information knowledge graph, making it more convenient to access tender information. In addition, for small samples of tender information data, this paper proposes an entity relationship triple extraction method based on transfer learning (TL)+BERT+CRF to extract triples from tender information, and stores the extracted knowledge in a Neo4j graph database, building a domain visualization knowledge graph. With the use of named entity recognition and template matching based on the knowledge graph, a tender information question-answering system is formed. The experimental results demonstrate that the triple extraction method adopted in this study shows significantly improved extraction performance compared to the BERT+CRF and BERT+BiLSTM+CRF models in the self-constructed tender information dataset. Furthermore, the question-answering system can also meet users’ needs for tender information queries.

articleTitle: Iteration-Aware Dynamic Quantization Neural Belief Propagation Decoder
publicationTitle: 2024 7th World Conference on Computing and Communication Technologies (WCCCT)
abstract: For some linear codes, neural networks have been found to be a way to enhance traditional belief propagation (BP) decoder. When deploying such methods in practice, quantization issues also need to be considered. Considering that the messages of variable/check nodes are variable during the BP decoding process, this paper proposes a dynamic quantization method to predict the optimal bit-width for the node’s message quantization in different decoding iterations. We build a shallow neural network as a bit-width predictor and train it jointly with a neural belief propagation decoding network. During actual decoding, the bit prediction network will generate appropriate bit-width for quantizing the messages of each layer of nodes. Finally, simulation experiments validate the effectiveness of the proposed quantization method.

articleTitle: Dual-Polarized Wideband Dipole Patch Antenna with Low Gain Variation for N257/N258 Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 7th World Conference on Computing and Communication Technologies (WCCCT)
abstract: In this paper, a dual-polarized wideband dipole patch antenna is proposed, which can be applied to the N257/N258 millimeter-wave band. For each polarization, the current can be regarded as the current generated by the driven dipole in the main polarized direction, and the energy is also coupled to the parasitic rings. On the contrary, the currents cancel each other in the direction of cross-polarization (X-pol), achieving a good X-pol level. Simulation results show that the −10-dB bandwidths of V-polarization and H-polarization are 31.10% (23.68-32.40 GHz) and 31.76% (23.86-32.87 GHz), respectively, and the isolation level between the dual ports is greater than 25 dB. Notably, by adding notched rings around the split dipole, the direction of the current can be changed, resulting in a stable gain of 8.5±0.5 dBi for port 1. In conclusion, the proposed antenna can potentially be applied in millimeter-wave (mm-Wave) communication system.

articleTitle: Formal Verification Method for Fault Coverage Capability of March Algorithm based on SpinalHDL
publicationTitle: 2024 7th World Conference on Computing and Communication Technologies (WCCCT)
abstract: March algorithm is a series of algorithms commonly used for memory testing, aiming to detect and diagnose faults in memory. The continuously evolving March algorithms are capable of detecting an increasing number of complex faults. However, the question of whether March algorithm can achieve the intended design goal, i.e., achieving full coverage of theoretically detectable faults, currently lacks practical validation methods. One approach to address this issue is to conduct formal verification of the fault detection capability of March algorithm on a software platform. Therefore, this paper proposes a method that utilizes SpinalHDL to model the fault behavior of memory cells and March algorithm. By simulating the progression of March algorithm within the memory cells, reaching sensitization conditions during the progression, injecting faults into the memory cells, and checking whether March algorithm can detect these faults, the fault detection capability of March algorithm can be validated to determine if it meets the design expectations.

articleTitle: Design of Microstrip-Based Power Divider Phase Shifter for 700-960 MHz Band
publicationTitle: 2024 7th World Conference on Computing and Communication Technologies (WCCCT)
abstract: This paper presents a phase shifter with low insertion loss and stable power distribution performance operated in the 2G/5G dual lower frequency bands of 700-790 MHz and 890-960 MHz. The microstrip lines are located on both sides of the dielectric substrate, with a sliding piece covering the microstrip lines, and an outer layer comprised of an aluminum metal shell serving as a ground plane. The power fluctuations of the phase shifter at frequencies ranging from 700 to 790 MHz, and from 890 to 960 MHz at each output port is within ±0.5 dB, with a maximum phase difference of approximately 75° between adjacent ports. To shorten the length of the phase-shifting section and improve spatial utilization efficiency, 1-mm wide curved microstrip lines are used in the phase-shifting section. Experimental results show that when the phase shifts are 37.5° and 75°, the phase difference variation between adjacent ports for each frequency band is within 20°, indicating good phase dispersion.

articleTitle: Design and Application of Aeropace Intelligent Housing System of Manned Space Station Base on Space-Integrated-Ground Network
publicationTitle: 2024 7th World Conference on Computing and Communication Technologies (WCCCT)
abstract: China manned space engineering has made many breakthroughs in manned space area and successfully completed the construction of China Space Station. During long-term operation of the space station in orbit, astronaut living and work become more and more important. In this paper, the design and application of the intelligent housing system of China Space Station based on space-integrated-ground network are described. And the future development about technology of aerospace intelligent housing system is forecasted.

articleTitle: Analysis of the use of social networks for the decision of the vote in an electoral campaign
publicationTitle: 2024 7th World Conference on Computing and Communication Technologies (WCCCT)
abstract: The problems in deciding the popular vote in electoral campaigns are constant in all countries of the world, especially in underdeveloped ones. The objective of this research is to analyze the use of social networks to decide the vote in an electoral campaign in different scenarios. The deductive method and exploratory research were used to analyze the information from the reference and the different websites. It turned out to be main actors for the execution of a social network in an electoral campaign and indicators supported by the contributions of the authors. It was concluded that social networks play an important role in decision-making in a political campaign for local or national elections, considering that these decisions can be falsely misleading, and that the people will be affected in the future.

articleTitle: Energy Efficient Algorithm for Multi-User Adaptive Edge Computing Offloading in Vehicular Networks Based on Meta Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 7th World Conference on Computing and Communication Technologies (WCCCT)
abstract: In the evolving Internet of Vehicles (IoV) landscape, the dual demands of low-latency and high computational power pose significant challenges, especially given the limited computational capabilities of internet-enabled autonomous vehicles and latency issues in cloud computing. This study proposes a novel, energy-efficient algorithm for multi-user adaptive edge computing offloading in vehicular networks, designed to optimize computational resource allocation. This reduces vehicle energy consumption while managing latency in a multi-user environment. At the heart of this strategy is a meta-reinforcement learning-based framework, adept at addressing the dynamic and complex nature of IoV environments. It uniquely integrates a directed acyclic graph with a model-independent meta-learning architecture, thereby enhancing the task offloading process’s efficiency and adaptability. This allows the system to rapidly adjust to environmental changes with minimal data, facilitating the development and implementation of efficient offloading strategies for edge computing. These strategies are crucial in significantly reducing energy consumption and maintaining latency performance across various user scenarios. Empirical assessments of this algorithm highlight its effectiveness in reducing energy usage and optimizing training latency, effectively balancing the energy-latency trade-off in IoV applications. The results indicate a significant advancement in computational resource management for multi-user vehicular networks.

articleTitle: Coordinated Attacks Detection Simulation With Deep Neural Network Algorithm and Federated Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 7th World Conference on Computing and Communication Technologies (WCCCT)
abstract: This research is focused on comparing the performance of Deep Neural Network (DNN) in Centralized Learning (CL) and Federated Learning (FL) concepts on simulating coordinated attack detection, such as Benign (normal activity), PortScan, DDoS, and Bot using the cicids2017 dataset for model training. The data preprocessing used is the Adaptive Synthetic Sampling (ADASYN) method for unbalanced data balancing. This research aims to advance the concept of network attack detection in an effort to keep each device’s data safe, without the need to send datasets to a central device to update the attack classification model, i.e. the data is trained in a decentralized way using the FL concept. In the simulation of coordinated attack detection, the result of FL is higher than that of CL. To achieve good attack classification results, the FL concept only required 20.45 seconds per epoch, which is shorter than the time required by the CL concept to train the attack classification model. Some of the advantages of the FL concept allow for smarter modeling, low latency, and less power consumption, while ensuring the privacy of each device’s data.

articleTitle: An Incremental Inverse-Free Augmented Complex-Valued Extreme Learning Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 7th World Conference on Computing and Communication Technologies (WCCCT)
abstract: The complex-valued extreme learning machine (CELM) is a powerful method for complex-valued signal processing. However, the optimal network structure of CELM is usually obtained by try and error, which is very time-consuming. To gain optimal network structure, we propose an inverse-free incremental CELM based on regularization pseudo-inverse, and then extend it to deal with the generality of complex-valued signals by incorporating the conjugates of the hidden nodes into the learning process, which leads to an incremental extreme learning machine with augmented hidden layer based on regularized pseudo-inverse. Simulation results demonstrate that both the proposed algorithms provide better generalization performance and reduced computational complexity, confirming their effectiveness.

articleTitle: Metasurface-Integrated Graphene-Based Patch Antenna for Wideband THz Communication and Sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 7th World Conference on Computing and Communication Technologies (WCCCT)
abstract: A graphene-based patch antenna for terahertz (THz) applications is proposed in this article. In order to optimize its performance, a metasurface is incorporated and affixed to the radiating patch by a distance of 2 $\mu$m. The graphene-based metasurface patch antenna with an overall size of $40\times 40 \times 8.1627$ $\mu$m3 exhibits a broad frequency bandwidth, ranging from 5.6 to 6.4 THz. The reflection coefficient is consistently below −10 dB across the entire frequency range, with a notable decrease of −22.28 dB at 6.25 THz. The proposed antenna shows excellent potential in THz communication, sensing, and imaging due to its wide bandwidth of 0.8 THz (13.3%).

articleTitle: Deep Learning Based Network intrusion detection for unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)
publicationTitle: 2024 7th World Conference on Computing and Communication Technologies (WCCCT)
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) have witnessed significant growth in various applications, including surveillance, reconnaissance, and data collection. However, the increased reliance on network connectivity exposes UAVs to potential cyber threats. Network intrusion detection systems (NIDS) are critical for safeguarding UAV communication channels. This paper presents a novel approach to enhance the security of UAV networks using deep learning-based NIDS. The proposed system leverages the capabilities of deep neural networks to detect and classify network intrusions effectively. We explore the utilization of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and recurrent neural networks (RNNs) for feature extraction and sequence modeling, respectively. The network is trained on a comprehensive dataset that simulates various attack scenarios to ensure robust detection performance. Our experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the deep learning-based NIDS for UAVs. The system achieves high detection accuracy and low false-positive rates, making it suitable for real-world applications. Furthermore, the model exhibits adaptability to evolving attack techniques, as it can continuously learn and improve its detection capabilities. The proposed deep learning-based NIDS not only enhances the cybersecurity of UAVs but also contributes to the overall safety and reliability of UAV operations. As UAVs become increasingly integrated into critical infrastructure and autonomous systems, the importance of robust network security measures cannot be overstated. This research represents a significant step towards ensuring the integrity and security of UAV networks in a rapidly evolving digital landscape.

articleTitle: Application of Active Learning Strategies in Fault Detection and Diagnosis within Communication Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 7th World Conference on Computing and Communication Technologies (WCCCT)
abstract: As wireless networks become extensively utilized in modern society, network stability and service quality have emerged as critical issues. Network failure not only affects the user experience, but may also cause significant economic losses to operators. Therefore, it is particularly important to design efficient fault detection and diagnosis methods. This study introduces a novel framework for network fault detection and diagnosis—a communication network fault prediction method based on optimized support vector machine (SVM) and active learning. The framework incorporates clustering to reinforce the memorization of fault data features and combines it with active learning for data ranking. Based on this ranking, balance weights are adjusted to construct a balanced dataset for wireless communication faults. Finally, the balanced dataset is fed into an SVM model with a base classifier for data classification. Through experiments simulating real-world scenarios, the proposed model has been validated to significantly enhance the efficiency and accuracy of fault detection in a simulated wireless communication network environment. It demonstrates the potential to achieve favorable results in practical applications.

articleTitle: SDPMP: Inference Acceleration of CNN Models in Heterogeneous Edge Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 7th World Conference on Computing and Communication Technologies (WCCCT)
abstract: The deployment of neural network models to edge devices for task inference is becoming increasingly common. However, due to network bandwidth and computing capability limitations, a single edge device is often insufficient to meet the inference delay requirements of computation-intensive tasks and continuous inference tasks with high load demands. To address this issue, we propose an efficient collaborative distributed inference acceleration framework that offloads tasks to multiple edge devices for parallel execution. The framework takes into account the speed of inference performed by heterogeneous edge devices and combines the principles of pipeline parallelism and the partial dependence characteristics of CNN intra-layer partitions. It also performs intelligent inter-layer and intra-layer partitions to maximize the throughput of continuous task inference and meet the requirements of low single task inference delay. We propose self-adaptive dynamic programming for model partition algorithm (SDPMP) to achieve this. Simulation results indicate that our proposed strategy significantly improves throughput compared to other classical algorithms.

articleTitle: Minimum Strong Radius of the Strong Product of Cycles and Odd Paths
publicationTitle: 2024 7th World Conference on Computing and Communication Technologies (WCCCT)
abstract: In the Internet, the effectiveness of information transmission depends directly on the transmission path. Determining the shortest transmission path is the core element to improve the efficiency of information transmission. The minimum strong radius, as an important parameter for measuring the shortest directed path in directed networks, becomes a key criterion for evaluating the performance of information transmission in the Internet. In this paper, we utilize the strong product of graphs to construct large-scale networks by using cycles and paths as factor graphs. By analyzing the relationship between the topological parameters of these factor graphs, we determine the exact value of the minimum strong radius of the strong product of cycles and odd paths under $m\gt n\geq 3$. In addition, we give upper and lower bounds on the minimum strong radius in the $3\leq m\gt n$ and $m=n\geq 4$ cases.

articleTitle: Cost Optimization for In-Network Computing Services Deployment in Edge-Cloud Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 7th World Conference on Computing and Communication Technologies (WCCCT)
abstract: In edge-cloud computing networks, clients can conveniently offload their computation tasks to the servers along the traffic flow, the process of which is known as in-network computing (INC). Notably, within the landscape of cutting-edge artificial intelligence, big data, and virtualization techniques, the computational demands of an INC service can range from relatively modest demands, for instance, image processing, to highly demanding tasks, such as generative pre-training. Since the edge-cloud computing networks’ pricing structure is associated with computational resources availability and the service location, a compelling quandary emerges concerning the deployment of INC services in edge-cloud networks. In this work, our focal point is the optimization of the cost-effectiveness pertaining to the deployment of INC services in edge-cloud computing networks. To begin, we mathematically formalize the In-Network Computing services Deployment (INCD) problem with the objective of cost optimization. In addressing the INCD problem, we propose an efficient heuristic algorithm known as Optimal In-Network Computing Services Deployment (Opt-INCD), which is proved to be optimal when deploying an INC service. Extensive simulation results show that the proposed Opt-INCD algorithm outperforms the greedy-based benchmarks by an average of 35.42% and 43.46%, respectively.

articleTitle: Enhancing Offloading Reliability for C-V2X: An Integrated Vertical and Horizontal Collaborative Offloading System
publicationTitle: 2024 7th World Conference on Computing and Communication Technologies (WCCCT)
abstract: With the rapid development of the intelligent transportation system, an increasing number of computation-intensive and delay-sensitive tasks are emerging in vehicular networks. Task offloading based on Vehicular Edge Computing (VEC), as an effective technology, is introduced to handle these tasks. However, vehicle mobility may lead to offloading link instability, causing interruptions that render the process unreliable and increase delay. In the Cellular Vehicle-to-Everything (C-V2X) scenario, this paper proposes an Integrated Vertical and Horizontal Collaborative (IVHC) offloading system to address task offloading interruptions. The system comprises two strategies: vertical collaborative and horizontal collaborative offloading, which address interruptions through cooperation in different offloading modes and VEC collaboration inter-cells, respectively. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed system effectively reduces the probability of offloading interruptions and enhances task offloading efficiency.

articleTitle: Chain Segment Protection for Dependence-aware Service Function Chain in NFV
publicationTitle: 2024 7th World Conference on Computing and Communication Technologies (WCCCT)
abstract: Network services can be delivered through a service function chain (SFC) for reliability-sensitive applications. Traditional SFC protection can be employed by providing a node-link-disjoint backup path to avoid SFC disruption. However, such a backup path may not exist in the network with limited resources. In this work, we propose a chain segment protection, which can effectively protect an SFC using several backup chain segments when a node-link-disjoint backup path is not available. We investigate how to jointly embed and provide chain segment protection while reducing the backup bandwidth resources. We define this problem as SFC failure with chain segment protection (SFCF-CSP), which is proved to be NP-hard. To address SFCF-CSP, we propose an efficient heuristic algorithms called backup chain-segment embedding and protection (BCEP). The simulation results show that the proposed algorithm outperforms the approaches that are directly extended from the existing work.

articleTitle: Monkey King: An Enhanced Asynchronous Consensus Protocol with Provable Security
publicationTitle: 2024 7th World Conference on Computing and Communication Technologies (WCCCT)
abstract: The asynchronous consensus protocol, as one of the core technologies of the blockchain, can ensure that the nodes in the system can agree on a certain value or status without assuming network capabilities. However, existing asynchronous consensus protocols face problems such as low efficiency and limited scalability. To address these problems, we propose an asynchronous consensus algorithm based on sharding, i.e., Monkey King, which innovatively introduces sharding into the field of asynchronous consensus. Our protocol divides the network into fixed-size shards, runs asynchronous common subset protocol (ACS) in each shard, selects a node from each shard to form the mainchain, then runs ACS once on the mainchain, and finally broadcasts the consensus result to All nodes. We implement the MK protocol and test the performance of different shard numbers under 100 nodes. Finally, we conduct comparative experiments between our protocol and Dumbo1/Dumbo2 under different numbers of nodes. Experimental results show that under 100-node scenario, the latency of our protocol is reduced by 94.51% and 79.04% respectively compared to Dumbo1 and Dumbo2. At the same time, under the condition of 100 nodes and a batch size of 10000, the throughput of our protocol increases by 520.1% and 12.7% respectively compared to Dumbo1 and Dumbo2, which reflects that our protocol has better performance in multi-node scenarios.

articleTitle: Identity/location Separation-based Mobility Management Mechanism for 5G HetNets
publicationTitle: 2024 7th World Conference on Computing and Communication Technologies (WCCCT)
abstract: The emergence of 5G networks has led to a significant increase in the number of base stations, resulting in smaller network coverage areas for individual base stations. The presence of various heterogeneous access nodes further exacerbates the situation, as the time for handover signal interactions becomes shorter. Traditional mobile management mechanisms, however, lack comprehensive considerations and are prone to issues such as low switch efficiency. Therefore, this paper proposes a mobile management mechanism based on identity-location separation. By utilizing identity and routing identifiers, this approach addresses the strong coupling issues of Internet Protocol (IP), effectively mitigating problems associated with mobile anchor points and reducing signaling overhead. To maintain mobility in access networks, this study introduces Multi-Access Edge Computing (MEC) technology. By acquiring additional contextual information, the proposed mechanism executes corresponding handover decision algorithms, including residence time predictions within small cell clusters and business-driven network access selection. Simulation results validate the superiority of the proposed mechanism over traditional cellular handover mechanisms.

articleTitle: Beamforming Design of Dual Intelligent Reflecting Surface Aided ISAC System Based on Cramér-Rao Bound Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 7th World Conference on Computing and Communication Technologies (WCCCT)
abstract: This paper investigates the design of joint transmit and reflective beamforming for dual intelligent reflecting surfaces (IRSs) aided integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) system. We aim to minimize the Cramér-Rao bound (CRB) for the direction of arrival (DOA) estimation of a target in the non-line-of-sight (NLOS) scenario while satisfying the per-user signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) constraints. One IRS is used to support NLOS sensing and communication functions simultaneously, while the other only assists the communication function of the system. Considering that the optimization problem is non-convex, we adopt semidefinite relaxation (SDR) and successive convex approximation (SCA) methods to iteratively solve the transmit beamformers and the reflection coefficients of two IRSs in the framework of alternating optimization. Simulation results indicate that the proposed scheme is more effective than the benchmark scheme.

articleTitle: MN-GAT: Incorporating Metric Names into Metric Correlation Graphs for Anomaly Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 7th World Conference on Computing and Communication Technologies (WCCCT)
abstract: Multivariate time series anomaly detection plays an essential role in various domains. Multiple metrics within the same system are not independent but exhibit specific correlations. Accurately characterizing the correlational relationships is the key issue in conducting multiple metrics analysis. In recent years, graph neural networks have shown outstanding performance in anomaly detection by effectively modeling the correlations among metrics. The challenge lies in accurately representing the interrelationships among metrics using graph structures. Existing approaches depend solely on the temporal patterns of metric time series, neglecting the information embedded in the metric names. In fact, metric names provide concise and meaningful information about the metrics and their relationships of. Therefore, this paper proposes a Metric Name (MN) assisted multi-metric graph attention-based (GAT) anomaly detection model, i.e., MN-GAT. This model automatically constructs a multi-metric correlation graph structure based on the multivariate time series and their names, and performs anomaly detection based on this correlation graph. The attention weights contained in the graph provide explanations for anomalies. Experimental results demonstrate that our method accurately models the interrelationships among metrics and achieves more accurate anomaly detection than baseline methods. Furthermore, it can assist operations personnel in identifying the root causes of failures and troubleshooting.

articleTitle: Using Parallel Branch-and-Bound Method to Accelerate Solving Mixed Integer Linear Programming
publicationTitle: 2024 7th World Conference on Computing and Communication Technologies (WCCCT)
abstract: The Branch-and-Bound(B&B) algorithm is an effective method for solving the Mixed Integer Linear Programming (MILP) problem. Its performance significantly impacts the overall performance of the MILP solver Additionally, parallelizing the B&B algorithm can further speed up solver efficiency. In this paper, a novel B&B parallel algorithm is proposed to accelerate the solution process of MILP problems. A Master-Worker parallel structure is employed in this algorithm, fully leverages the serial performance of the solver. To minimize overhead, only necessary information is shared between the Master and Worker to utilizing shared memory communication. During the search of the B&B tree, the Master distributes problem nodes to Workers. Workers calculate problem nodes to update the information and subsequently return a sequence of new sub-problem nodes to the Master. Once optimality is achieved or the Master has no more problem nodes, the solution process is concluded. This research demonstrates that the proposed B&B parallel algorithm exhibits excellent acceleration performance. Research indicate that the B&B parallel algorithm presented in this study exhibits a substantial speedup factor of 1.53 for instances with over 10,000 nodes within the MIPLIB2017 benchmark. Furthermore, it demonstrates an even more impressive speedup factor of up to 2.53 for instances with more than 60,000 nodes, thereby underscoring excellent performance. It is noteworthy that the relationship between the speedup factor and the number of threads is predominantly linear.

articleTitle: Resource Allocation Strategies for Cloud-Edge-End Collaboration in Heterogeneous Edge Computing
publicationTitle: 2024 7th World Conference on Computing and Communication Technologies (WCCCT)
abstract: With the continuous innovation of information technology, the Internet of Everything (IoE) is gradually being realized, and more IoT application scenarios have increasingly urgent requirements for high-performance computing and low-latency response. To address the bottleneck of insufficient computing power and energy constraints of terminal devices, edge computing can effectively enhance the task processing capability of terminal devices and improve service quality. However, existing edge computing network architectures, which often provide a single edge server computing capability based on terrestrial networks, cannot meet the task offloading requirements of terminal devices in ubiquitous network environments. This paper designs a cloud-edge-end collaboration space-air-ground integration multi-layer edge computing network architecture (CEEC-SAGIN), and based on this architecture, a heterogeneous network system of terminal devices, multi-layer edge computing services and cloud computing services are constructed. Then, a task processing model is constructed with the optimization objective of minimizing the task processing delay of the system, taking into account the task offloading ratio, computational resources and transmission resources involved in the task processing process of the terminal devices of the system. Further, a multi-layer task offloading and resource allocation algorithm (MTORA) is proposed to realize the optimal allocation of resources in system task processing. Finally, simulation experiments show that the CEEC-AGIN architecture proposed in this paper can meet the requirements of more applications, and the proposed model can improve the system task processing efficiency by up to roughly 15% and reduce the system task processing latency by up to approximately 10% compared with other resource allocation strategies.

articleTitle: A Privacy-Preservation-Based Secured Model for Detection Network Crawlers
publicationTitle: 2024 7th World Conference on Computing and Communication Technologies (WCCCT)
abstract: Crawler detection is crucial for Network Service Provider (NSP), and the federated learning-based approach to crawler detection has been under vigorous investigation. Nevertheless, training crawler detection models locally with NSP training server-side data is ineffective and expose privacy risks. To address this problem, we propose a privacy-preserving and communication-efficient model for decentralized federated learning by combining NSP training server-side and central server-side aggregation. Specifically, we developed an enhanced federated learning algorithms to train the model, avoiding data transfer burdens. We design perturbed local model parameters and corresponding method to mitigate privacy risks during upload. We developed an innovative data processing algorithm that effectively enables the server to obtain structured data with spatiotemporal information by analyzing user access time and resources. Finally, we improved the time series detection model by fusing the output of each time step with the hidden layer, effectively improve the robustness of the detection model. Evaluation on two datasets under two network crawler scenarios shows substantial improvement of accuracy while ensuring privacy protection.

articleTitle: Non-uniform Node Dynamic Deployment Clustering Algorithm Based on Virtual Force
publicationTitle: 2024 7th World Conference on Computing and Communication Technologies (WCCCT)
abstract: In Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs), node deployment and partition strategy are two important aspects to evaluate network performance. Although many existing deployment and partitioning algorithms have achieved the goal of averaging node distribution and optimizing network structure, for the uneven distribution of energy and information in non-uniform networks, it is easy to lead to significant shortening of network lifespan and premature occurrence of energy holes and other issues. Taking into account the aforementioned drawbacks, this paper puts forth a Virtual Force-based Non-uniform Node Dynamic Deployment And Clustering Algorithm(VFNDDCA). On the basis of the virtual force algorithm, the force models of different grids on nodes under different energy consumption levels are designed. This algorithm dynamically deploys nodes according to changes in energy coverage to optimize network performance, and makes reasonable partitions according to the deployed node distribution to optimize the energy supply mechanism. Simulation results demonstrate the algorithm’s ability to significantly extend network lifespan, achieve load balancing, avoid energy holes and reduce node energy consumption in non-uniform networks.

articleTitle: A Segmented Off-Grid Near-Field Wideband Channel Estimation Approach for XL-MIMO
publicationTitle: 2024 7th World Conference on Computing and Communication Technologies (WCCCT)
abstract: With the coming of the 6G era, extremely large-scale multiple-input-multiple-output (XL-MIMO) will be one of the key technologies in the near future. By that time, the number of antennas in a base station (BS) will have increased to hundreds or even thousands. In addition, terahertz (THz) and millimeter wave bands will also be widely used in 6G due to their excellent performance. According to electromagnetic theory, the Rayleigh distance increases as the number of antenna aperture and the frequency increase. This means that the near-field distance expands. However, accurate near-field wideband channel estimation is very difficult, both the beam split effect and the recovery of both distance and angle dimensions have to be taken into consideration. To solve this problem, inspired by the traditional near-field narrowband channel estimation algorithm. We propose a segmented off-grid polar-domain simultaneous iterative gridless weighted (St-P-SIGW) algorithm to estimate the wideband channel, which not only considers the beam split effect but also can efficiently improve the estimation accuracy. At the end of this paper, we compare the proposed algorithm with other algorithms. simulation result shows that the algorithm in this paper achieves better results.

articleTitle: A Secure Convolutional Neural Network Inference Model Based on Homomorphic Encryption
publicationTitle: 2024 7th World Conference on Computing and Communication Technologies (WCCCT)
abstract: The utilization of convolutional neural network (CNN) inference models has gained widespread adoption across various domains; however, it raises concerns regarding user privacy and security due to the requirement of plaintext information during the inference process. Homomorphic encryption has been proposed as a viable solution to address CNN’s security issues. Nevertheless, this encryption algorithm encounters certain limitations such as significant ciphertext expansion, restricted nonlinear computing power, and limited number of multiplications, which hinder its application in CNN inference models. In this paper, we present an inference model framework that leverages the single instruction multiple data and ciphertext rotation functions of homomorphic encryption along with the additive secret sharing (ASS) concept to design and transform each network layer of CNN. Our approach effectively mitigates ciphertext expansion rate while enhancing computational efficiency and reducing communication volume without compromising on inference accuracy.

articleTitle: A Survey Of Automatic Fact Verification Research
publicationTitle: 2024 7th World Conference on Computing and Communication Technologies (WCCCT)
abstract: With the evolution of social media technology, the mode of information exchange has transitioned from a singular text format to a multifaceted blend of text, images, audio, and video. This transformation has given rise to the proliferation of multimodal false information, sparking widespread concern across diverse sectors of society. This paper takes a fact-checking perspective, offering a comprehensive review of pertinent research in the field. It commences by introducing prevalent datasets used in contemporary fact-checking. Subsequently, a detailed analysis of fact-checking methods and multimodal detection techniques, centered around the FEVER dataset, is presented, accompanied by comparative insights into various approaches. Finally, the paper delves into the anticipated challenges faced by fact-checking methods in the future.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Based Prediction on Relapse of Acute Myeloid Leukemia
publicationTitle: 2024 7th World Conference on Computing and Communication Technologies (WCCCT)
abstract: -Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is a high-incidence adult acute leukemia. Most patients will relapse after remission and turn into refractory and relapsed acute leukemia. This study aims at employing machine learning algorithms to develop a relapse prediction model for AML patients. Based on the AML patient data provided by the TARGET project from Meshinchi Laboratory of the National Institutes of Health (NIH) Cancer Research Center, we first normalize all samples to meet the requirements of the machine learning model. To eliminate the accuracy loss of the prediction model caused by category imbalance, we further use the synthetic minority over-sampling technique (SMOTE) to oversample the normalized data. Finally, we utilize the training datasets to develop three typical prediction models, namely Gaussian kernel support vector machine (G-SVM), linear kernel support vector machine (L-SVM), and decision tree (DT). The experiment results show that the data processed by SMOTE-based over-sampling can significantly improve the performances of the three prediction models, and the holistic performance of the G-SVM model is superior to another, which can be applied to the diagnosis and treatment decisions to assist clinicians in taking early intervention measures for AML patients.

articleTitle: Resource Allocation for SFC Networks: A Deep Reinforcement Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 7th World Conference on Computing and Communication Technologies (WCCCT)
abstract: The rapid evolution of mobile communications technology has led to the widespread adoption of cutting-edge technologies such as Network Function Virtualization (NFV) and Software-Defined Networking (SDN). Network flexibility and scalability have been greatly improved by virtualizing traditional dedicated hardware functions on standard hardware and servers. However, the effective deployment of Service Function Chains (SFC) and the allocation of computing resources in this virtualized network environment remain to be solved. This study presents a resource allocation approach using the Proximal Policy optimization (PPO) algorithm. It features a novel SFC network model, utilizing reinforcement learning to intelligently train and make decisions, focusing on the cost-performance relationship in node deployment. Simulation results show that this algorithm effectively balances the relationship between node deployment cost and end-to-end service latency while ensuring the quality of service requirements.

articleTitle: GAN-Assisted Sample Equalization for CNN-Based Human Peripheral Leukocyte Image Recognition and Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 7th World Conference on Computing and Communication Technologies (WCCCT)
abstract: Morphology analysis and the count of distinct cells in human peripheral blood are dominant methods to diagnose common blood diseases. In recent years, with the purpose of improving the efficiency of these methods, the convolutional neural network (CNN), a widely used model of artificial intelligence technology, has been utilized in computer-aided blood tests to recognize and classify blood cell images. However, due to the nature of a smaller number of leukocytes in one blood sample, the CNN model is generally trained by insufficient leukocyte images and thus shows lower accuracy on leukocytes. To address the above issue, we propose a generative adversarial network (GAN) assisted framework to increase leukocyte images and further enable the CNN model to improve the performance of human peripheral leukocyte image recognition and classification. We validate the effectiveness of the proposed framework through a comparative performance analysis of four CNN models trained by four image datasets deriving from different sample equalization methods. The numerical results show that the GAN-assisted sample equalization method is superior to making the CNN model converge fast and attain high recognition and classification accuracy.

articleTitle: DQN-based Network Selection and Load Balancing for LEO Satellite-Terrestrial Integrated Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 7th World Conference on Computing and Communication Technologies (WCCCT)
abstract: The future communication system will involve collaboration between satellites and terrestrial stations. UEs that directly communicate with low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites will experience frequent handovers, which necessitate effective mobility management for user terminals within the LEO satellite-terrestrial integrated network. This paper proposes a deep Q-learning network (DQN) controller based on the Markov decision process (MDP) to address this issue. This controller can be utilized for adaptive resource allocation and network selection in satellite-terrestrial integrated networks to optimize communication resource utilization and achieve load balancing.

articleTitle: Inserting Pre-Cached Ads into Short Video Lists for Improved Users’ Watching Experience
publicationTitle: 2024 7th World Conference on Computing and Communication Technologies (WCCCT)
abstract: With the rapid development of short video field, it is common to insert advertisements among short videos. However, since both ordinary short videos (OSVs) and advertisement short videos (ASVs) are currently transmitted from the server, the transmission of ASVs consumes too much network bandwidth resources due to the high-bitrate of ASVs, resulting in large startup delays for all videos. To solve this problem, drawing inspiration from splash-screen advertising, we propose pre-caching ASVs on the client, i.e., when the network quality is good, the client pre-caches some ASVs and then inserts them into the list of OSVs pushed from the server. In this way, ASVs can be played directly without involving network transmission, and furthermore, viewing pre-cached ASVs can help restore the network transmission capacity and alleviate the startup delays of subsequent videos. In this context, we study how to insert pre-cached ASVs to maximize the user experience, where the user experience takes into account the impact of startup delay and advertisement gap. We build an optimization model to maximize the user experience and design a greedy genetic algorithm (GGA) to address the challenge posed by the huge search space of the ad insertion problem. GGA firstly establishes an initial set of ad insertion positions, where each position indicates how ASVs are inserted into the OSVs list to create a new playlist. Secondly, GGA uses a genetic algorithm to iteratively performs mutations on the ad insertion positions, while using a greedy algorithm to determine the specific placement of each ASV. During each iteration, the user experience value of the playlist corresponding to each ad insertion position is calculated, and some individuals with the best user experience value are selected for genetic mutation until reaching the maximum number of iterations, and eventually we can get the playlist with the best user experience. Finally, simulation results show that our GGA can significantly optimize user experience compared to baseline algorithms.

articleTitle: Channel Estimation Method Based on Training Sequence Optimization in Mobility Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2024 7th World Conference on Computing and Communication Technologies (WCCCT)
abstract: In wireless communication systems assisted by Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface (RIS), Channel Situation Information (CSI) is the prerequisite and foundation for effectively regulating beamforming. A training sequence optimization channel estimation method based on Kalman filtering is proposed for RIS assisted MISO communication systems under time-varying conditions. Firstly, the Linear Minimum Mean Squared Error (LMMSE) method is used to estimate the CSI of the cascaded channel. Secondly, based on the obtained CSI, the reflection matrix of RIS and the training sequence transmitted by the base station were jointly optimized to minimize the mean square error of the original channel estimation. Finally, in order to fully utilize the temporal correlation of the channel, prior information of the channel was considered, and Kalman filter (KF) was adopted to further improve the accuracy of channel estimation. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed channel estimation method has better performance compared to various benchmark methods.

articleTitle: QUIC Traffic Classification Based on Multi-Feature Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 7th World Conference on Computing and Communication Technologies (WCCCT)
abstract: Traffic classification is of great significance to network management and security. However, with the QUIC (Quick UDP Internet Connection) full encryption protocol launched by Google, the lack of plaintext information has brought enormous challenges to traffic classification. Existing research primarily focuses on utilizing machine learning methods to explore flow statistical features for the classification of QUIC traffic. However, due to the influence of encryption algorithms, packet size distortion will occur, making the classification accuracy poor and unable to be refined. Given the above problems, this paper proposes a multi-feature fusion classification method. By decrypting the initial packet of QUIC traffic, obtaining the plaintext information of the ClientHello field to extract category features, and integrating numerical flow statistical features and machine learning methods to make QUIC traffic classification more refined and precise. Through the captured QUIC traffic experiment, the fine-grained classification accuracy for QUIC traffic proposed in the paper reaches 99.95%.
